transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been concerning you?

Hi, Doctor. Thanks for seeing me. I came in because... well, I've been having a real problem with eating at night. 

After everyone goes to bed, I’ll go to the kitchen and tell myself I’m just having a few bites of leftovers. But then I sort of just keep going. Before I even realize it, I’ve eaten half a tray of catered pasta from work, the leftover dessert from a client dinner, and whatever snacks were sitting in the pantry. All in one sitting. It's been happening a lot, and it's really starting to concern me.
During these episodes when you're eating at night, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating, even if you wanted to?

Yes, that's exactly it. Once I start... especially if it's been a tense night with my husband... it just feels like the decision-making part of me goes completely offline. I'll just keep reaching for more food, even while I’m standing there thinking to myself, ‘Patricia, stop, this is enough.’ But I just can't seem to actually make myself stop.
After these nighttime eating episodes, do you do anything to try to counteract what you've eaten—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, exercising excessively, or restricting food the next day?

No, I don't do any of that. I've never made myself throw up or used laxatives. And I definitely don't exercise excessively... between work and everything else, I barely have time to get to the gym as it is. 

As for the next day, I don't really restrict my food either. I usually just wake up feeling awful and really guilty about what I did, but I still eat my regular meals. I just sort of... sit with the guilt, I guess. But no, I don't do anything to try and undo it.
How often would you say these nighttime eating episodes happen? Are we talking about a few times a week, every night, or something else?

I'd say... well, for the last three months or so, there’s been at least one night almost every week where I end up eating like this. It usually happens after an argument, or if I've had a late work event. And some weeks, it actually happens twice.

During these nighttime eating episodes, do you feel a sense of loss of control that's specific to just the eating—or do you also feel like you're losing control in other ways during those times, like emotionally or with other behaviors?

I think... it's really just the eating. I mean, I might be upset or stressed out, obviously, but I'm not losing control of my emotions or doing anything else out of the ordinary. I'm not yelling or breaking things or anything like that. 

It's really just the food. That's the one area where I feel like I completely lose my grip during those times.

These nighttime eating episodes and the guilt you feel afterward—how much do they affect your day-to-day life? For example, do they impact your work, your relationships, or how you feel about yourself?

Well, I'm still keeping up with work and everything. I haven't let it affect my job. But... it definitely affects how I feel about myself. The mornings after I do this, I just feel so drained and, honestly, really ashamed. 

It's starting to impact my personal time, too. I used to go to yoga or meet up with friends for creative projects, but lately, I've been skipping those plans. I just... I don't want to face anyone when I feel that way about myself. So, yeah, it's definitely taking a toll.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight since these nighttime eating episodes started happening more frequently?

I haven't really noticed any major changes, no. My clothes still fit about the same. I don't weigh myself very often, so I can't give you an exact number, but it doesn't seem like my weight has fluctuated much, if at all.

During these nighttime eating episodes while you're actually eating, do you feel distressed or upset about what you're doing in that moment, or does the bad feeling mainly come afterward when you realize how much you've eaten?

While I'm actually eating, I don't really feel upset. It's more of a... a zoning out, I guess. But afterward, that's when it hits me. I feel incredibly embarrassed and just disgusted with myself. I sit there and think about how I've completely blown it. I try so hard to be this disciplined person during the day, and then I ruin it. I just sit there thinking I should have gone for a run or done yoga instead of eating all that.
